statements.text: The Prime Minister said an energy ceasefire, with both sides stopping their attacks, is the quickest way to get diesel back onto world markets without rewarding the aggressor. He welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire, and said President Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would implement it immediately once a start date is confirmed.

At their meeting at Downing Street, the leaders underlined that Russia had no interest in peace. The Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, and the leaders discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support to Ukraine ahead of the winter.

The Prime Minister said the UK would continue to develop innovative military solutions for use on the battlefield in Ukraine, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted from other partners. He also said the UK would continue its diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.
Andy Burnham said supporting Ukraine is not just the right thing to do but the necessary thing to do, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent.

In recent days the government has announced new funding to help Ukraine get through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that covers over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity.

The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to provide urgent support to Ukraine in the coming weeks, and will accelerate delivery of critical air defence missiles.

The UK will accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which it says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. It has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of a £45 million missile package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter requirements.
The UK is delivering £45 million of surface-to-air missiles to Ukraine and is standing by plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian liquefied natural gas exports.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor John Healey is urging partners at the IMF meetings in Bangkok to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian LNG. He said he urges partners to back the ban, like the UK has, to curtail the war chest funding Putin so desperately wants.

The Prime Minister told the Commons the government assesses the RAF Fairford incident is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard. He said the government will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and bring further sanctions to restrict Iran's and the IRGC's capacity to do harm.

The Prime Minister confirmed Britain's decision to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling, and said a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions. He condemned the attacks on King Khalid International Airport and said Britain will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

A UK government spokesperson said Ukraine has repeatedly shown it is serious about peace, while Russia has repeatedly rejected full and partial ceasefires and continues attacks on Ukrainian civilians and energy. The spokesperson said Russia could end this war today.

The Prime Minister told the Commons that in the three weeks since his meeting with President Zelenskyy in New York, Russian strikes have intensified further, with more attacks on civilians, apartment blocks and buses carrying children.

The government says it remains committed to supporting Ukraine for as long as it takes and to working with partners toward a durable peace. Andy Burnham said the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes and will go further and faster in its support.

The Prime Minister confirmed the UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a food and drink trade deal, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a new youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration.

The Prime Minister said a food and drink trade deal would add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040, lift burdens of up to £1,400 on a single shipment for farmers and food producers, and end export health certificates costing up to £200 each time for small businesses. He said the proposed energy deal could cut wholesale energy costs in Northern Ireland by 20%.

The Prime Minister said the chances of a summit deal would be enhanced by being open to discussion of the UK's relationship with the EU in the longer term. He said that after the summit a serious dialogue on options should be set up, that the British public will be the boss at every stage, and that public opinion currently supports a pragmatic approach.

The Prime Minister said Russia is conducting a campaign of hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe. He said he and Chancellor Merz agreed in Berlin a new partnership to tackle these threats, and confirmed a new National Centre for Information Defence.
The Prime Minister said NATO is a defensive alliance that does not seek confrontation, but that resolve to defend allies is absolute, and that Britain will meet its NATO commitments in full.
The Prime Minister said Britain will place AI centre stage in its G20 presidency in 2027, and aims to work towards agreeing a single set of global principles and standards on AI during that year.

The Prime Minister said he raised the Falkland Islands with President Trump and the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British, and that the UK will always do whatever it takes to uphold the islanders' will.
In his Motherwell speech the Prime Minister said Scotland, the most devolved nation in the UK, is one of the most centralised nations in Europe.
The Prime Minister said the review led by Alan Milburn is challenging government to build a system based on the Easterhouse principle of names not numbers, built from the bottom up.

The Prime Minister said he wants a change in public procurement across the UK, working with the devolved governments. He said he wants all public procurement to back local manufacturing, citing buses for Greater Manchester that he had built by Alexander Dennis in Falkirk.
The Prime Minister said the Scottish government has agreed to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west.
The Prime Minister said around one in six young people in Scotland are not in education, employment or training, and that he will not have a country where people in their 20s are simply on benefits.

Great British Railways' headquarters will be at Becketwell in Derby, with construction expected to begin in early 2027 and completion by spring 2029. The government estimates a £151 million boost to Derby's economy and says the HQ will bring hundreds of rail jobs, and up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship.

Andy Burnham said people have put up with a railway that often lets them down, and that today is another big step forward. Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, with Great British Railways aiming for better services for passengers.

Pat McFadden said the government is determined to build the strong pipeline of skilled workers the rail sector depends on, and that the apprenticeship forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities.
Claire Ward called it fantastic news for Derby, and said she is delighted Great British Railways will be based in Derby, bringing hundreds of jobs.

The Prime Minister said he is making a serious and genuine offer to the Scottish Government, to design a new model of regional economic empowerment across Scotland in the months ahead. He offered DWP devolution, a localised employment support model similar to England's but shaped by Holyrood, and said the National Economic Council will meet the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in a couple of weeks.

Douglas Alexander said power was never supposed to stop at the doors of the Scottish Parliament, and that the Prime Minister's offer to the Scottish Government is a genuine one, with the Scotland Office ready to help make it happen. He said two governments with one goal could deliver good jobs and real opportunity in every corner of Scotland.

statements.text: Chancellor John Healey is pressing partners at the IMF meetings to step up support for Ukraine. Healey urged partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, like the UK has done, to curtail the war chest funding Putin. The Foreign Secretary did the same with partners at the Warsaw Security Forum.

The Prime Minister welcomed Zelenskyy to Downing Street on 14 October. The leaders reflected on their call and on Russia's attacks on civilians and energy since Trump called for an energy ceasefire, and underlined that Russia had no interest in peace. The Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, said the UK would continue developing innovative military solutions, and said it would discuss accelerating defensive support ahead of winter and continue its diplomatic efforts on international supplies of defensive equipment.

The Commons statement of 12 October says the UK and Germany agreed a new partnership to tackle Russian hybrid threats, that the UK will establish a new National Centre for Information Defence, and that Britain is open to Germany joining the Global Combat Air Programme alongside Italy and Japan.

Britain is sending air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling support, and a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions. The statement condemns the attacks on King Khalid International Airport and says Britain will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

The Prime Minister raised the Falkland Islands and the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British with President Trump, and says the UK will always do whatever it takes to uphold the islanders' will.

The Commons statement says NATO is a defensive alliance that does not seek confrontation, that the UK's resolve to defend its allies is absolute, and that the UK will meet its NATO commitments in full.
The UK takes up the G20 presidency in 2027 and will place AI centre stage, aiming to agree a single set of global principles and standards on AI during its presidency year.

The Prime Minister will invite the First Minister to work with him to push power out of Westminster and Holyrood, and to design a new model of regional economic empowerment for Scotland with the Scottish Government. In Motherwell on 16 October he said the National Economic Council will meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales and the First and Deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland to put the offer on the table.

Douglas Alexander said power was never supposed to stop at the doors of the Scottish Parliament, and that people in North Lanarkshire, Fife and the Highlands know what their communities need better than any minister. He called the Prime Minister's offer to the Scottish Government a genuine one, and said the Scotland Office is ready to help make it happen.

The Prime Minister will say Scotland, the most devolved nation in the UK, is one of the most centralised nations in Europe, and that the next stage of devolution should place more decision-making in the hands of Scotland's regions and cities to drive reindustrialisation.

The Prime Minister offers Scotland DWP devolution, a model of localised employment support shaped by Holyrood, based on the Easterhouse principle of names not numbers, and says the UK government should explore giving Scotland's regions powers over skills, transport, investment, infrastructure and housing.
The Prime Minister says around one in six young people in Scotland are not in education, employment or training, and that too many young people are missing out.

The headquarters of Great British Railways has been sited at Becketwell in Derby. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029. The site will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff, and an estimated £151 million boost is expected for the Derby economy with hundreds of rail jobs.

Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with first starters based in Derby. Pat McFadden said the apprenticeship will give young people the chance to explore career paths in the sector, and that it forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities.

Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, with Great British Railways bringing the railway together around one mission, better services for passengers, with Derby at the heart of its future.
Claire Ward said the news is fantastic for Derby, and that she is particularly pleased about the 600 apprenticeship places.
